faqs.q: How much does a Scottish Terrier cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $500–$2,000 for a Scottish Terrier puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: Budget $120–$200 per month for a Scottish Terrier, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Small breeds often cost less on food and some products, but vet bills don't proportionally reduce — procedures cost similar amounts regardless of size.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($300–600), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Scottish Terrier cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Scottish Terrier are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $1,500–$3,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Scottish Terriers shed a lot?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Scottish Terrier need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Scottish Terrier's wiry coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Scottish Terriers that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Scottish Terriers easy to train?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers are independent thinkers and can be challenging to train. They respond best to high-value rewards and clear, consistent criteria. A structured puppy class from week one is strongly recommended.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Scottish Terriers. Clicker training with precise timing works well to mark the exact moment of correct behaviour. Avoid aversive methods — they increase anxiety and often create secondary behavioural problems.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers can take longer to reach reliable obedience than easier-to-train breeds — expect 3–6 months of consistent daily training for solid basics. Their independent nature means results compound slowly but durably with patience.

faqs.q: What health problems do Scottish Terriers commonly have?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers are most commonly associated with blood clotting disorder and other breed-specific conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Scottish Terriers live?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers have an average lifespan of 12–12 years. Small breeds often live longer than large breeds. Dental care is particularly important for small dogs, as dental disease is a common longevity issue.

faqs.q: Are Scottish Terriers prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Hip dysplasia is less common in Scottish Terriers than in large working breeds, but it can still occur. Responsible breeders screen breeding stock. Keeping your Scottish Terrier at a healthy weight is the most effective preventive measure.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Scottish Terrier puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Scottish Terrier puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Scottish Terrier-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Scottish Terriers good with kids?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers can do well with children when properly socialised from puppyhood. Every dog is an individual — early exposure to children's behaviour (noise, sudden movements) is the most effective preparation.

faqs.q: Do Scottish Terriers get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers can be selective with other dogs due to their independent nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Scottish Terriers bark a lot?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers are not considered excessive barkers. They may alert to strangers or unusual sounds, but are generally manageable with basic training. Consistent "quiet" reinforcement from puppyhood keeps this in check.

faqs.q: Are Scottish Terriers good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers adapt reasonably well to apartment living, particularly if they receive consistent daily walks and indoor enrichment. Their compact nature makes them less disruptive in confined spaces than high-energy large breeds.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Scottish Terrier need per day?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Scottish Terriers good running partners?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Scottish Terrier doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Scottish Terrier be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Scottish Terrier depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A long-line is recommended as an intermediate step for several months.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: A Scottish Terrier needs approximately ½–1½ cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: Adult Scottish Terriers should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Scottish Terriers do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Scottish Terrier from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Small breeds typically transition to adult food around 12 months. Moving too late keeps them on higher-calorie puppy formulas that can cause weight gain in lower-activity adults.

faqs.q: Is a Scottish Terrier a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers can be challenging for first-time owners due to their independent temperament. Prior dog experience or professional training classes from the start significantly improves outcomes. Research the breed thoroughly before committing.

faqs.q: Are Scottish Terriers good family dogs?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers can be good family dogs when properly socialised. Their suitability depends more on individual temperament and upbringing than breed alone.

faqs.q: Do Scottish Terriers do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Scottish Terriers are more independent than many breeds and generally tolerate alone time better than highly social dogs. Still, aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone for an adult dog, and less for puppies.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Scottish Terrier?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Scottish Terrier — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
